{{reconstructed}}
==Proto-West Semitic==

===Etymology===
Reconstructed in Militarev & Kogan's ''Semitic Etymological Dictionary'' as {{m|sem-wes-pro||*paraš-}}, with a variant {{m|sem-wes-pro||*paras-}}. There is no trace of it in Akkadian or, notably, in Ugaritic. In Hebrew and Aramaic it mostly means “horseman”; according to the SED the Hebrew plural shows that {{m|hbo|פָּרָשׁ}} had been replaced by a derived {{m|sem-wes-pro||*parrāš-}} “horseman”. The Ethiopian Semitic and Modern South Arabian words are, following Sima, native rather than borrowed, while Harari {{m|har|ፈረዝ|tr=färäz}} and most Gurage forms in ''-z'' are loans from Cushitic or Omotic. Most of the similar words for “horse” in Chadic and Cushitic are thought to be borrowed from Arabic and Ethiopian Semitic.
